question: Does the typed band's advantage over the deep (and shallow) type-blind band survive (1) impact energies up to the generation-scale calibration (Willow median 2 MHz peak shift), (2) echoed instead of standard decoupling, (3) M1-style faster trapping on protected sites, (4) a JJ-Only 10 GHz protected gap?

model_changes.energy_scale: x0 (delivered dose) multiplied by energy_scale before the bridge; delivery is linear in energy, all nonlinearity (recombination, tunnelling) is downstream. Relative to the paper bank (0.01 x config energy range); x100 = config range on which generation_scale was solved.
model_changes.decoupling: passed to channels_from_site_design (Platform.decoupling); 'echo' uses the frozen power-law echo residual.
model_changes.trap_multiplier: trapping_hz of every non-weak site (protected ancillas AND data qubits) = base x multiplier; weak sites base.
model_changes.protected_gap: protected ancilla gap; data qubits stay 12 GHz. Hybrid (Willow f_q, mean gap), not an MIT device model.

layout_definitions: studies.family(d=9, f=0.3, T_M=9): shallow, deep (widest feasible type-blind band), typed_paper (= count sweep n168|typed)

trajectories.seed_rule: p1core.task_seed(78002, event, mode): shared by every condition (common random numbers across layouts AND physics settings)

endpoints.primary: eta = R(deep) / R(typed) per setting, R = impact-conditioned excess risk (worse input mode, stratified mean minus D0C quiet), 95% paired bootstrap percentile interval
secondary: excess risk per layout per setting
eta vs energy scale curve (std and echo)
endpoints.estimator: analyze_calext.py: B=4000, seed 20261108, Dirichlet(pool_counts+1), Jeffreys quiet draws (quiet_d9.json D0C), identical bootstrap indices for all conditions

order_and_looks: 1. Wave A0 (E1|standard, all three layouts). Look ONLY at the anchor: analyze_calext.py anchor.

2. Anchor PASS iff, for both typed and shallow, (a) the new point estimate lies in the count sweep's nominal 95% interval (typed [1.74e-4, 3.08e-4], shallow [5.00e-4, 1.06e-3]) AND (b) the 95% paired bootstrap interval of new minus count-sweep excess risk (same events, same estimator) contains 0. Bit-identity is NOT required: the count sweep ran on macOS arm64 and Stim seeded sampling is machine-dependent (CONTROL_REPRODUCTION.json).
3. Anchor FAIL -> stop and debug; no other setting is run or read.
4. Anchor PASS -> run waves A, B, C in that order without interim looks; analyse all settings together (analyze_calext.py all).

decision_rules.eta_resolved_gt1_at_x100_echo: Typed placement helps for Willow-scale impacts on a well-decoupled circuit (strongest claim).
decision_rules.eta_gt1_at_x1_to_x10_not_resolved_at_x10: Claim restricted to sub-threshold (small/medium) impacts; argue from their rate.
decision_rules.eta_gt1_at_x100_standard_not_echo: Large-impact advantage came from unechoed phase errors; the echo result is the device-relevant one.
decision_rules.trap_x10_changes_eta: Trapping and placement interact: 'changes sharply' = the trap-x10 eta interval excludes the matching trap-x1 echo point estimate (E1 and E100 separately).
decision_rules.jj_only_gap: Reported as a sensitivity point; same rule as trap_x10 against E1|echo.
